edition.status: The title page names the fifth edition of 1906 and the publisher and place of printing. The file opens with a Dante epigraph with Longfellow's translation (Longfellow died 1882), a Preface to the 'Home Education' Series, a Preface to the Fourth Edition dated Scale How, Ambleside, 1905, and the contents list, all in Mason's own voice apart from the epigraph. No introduction, notes or editing by another hand appear apart from the epigraph translation. The body is Parts I to VI, with footnotes. The workbook uses selected chapters only (see selection) and says so.

selection.rule: Home Education is a long book on bringing up children under nine. The workbook is a programme for a parent's own practice: time outdoors, looking, habit, attention, narration, the atmosphere of home and reading. Every exercise asks about the reader's own time, attention, observation and plan. None asks about a child's health, development or progress, and nothing in the workbook gives advice on those.
selection.length: Eight weeks, as in the catalogue (extended tier). Each week has 8 or 9 key ideas, 2 exercises and about 15 minutes in all. About 8,300 reader-facing words in total.

selection.chaptersUsed: Part I ch. 1; Part II ch. 1 to 5, 10, 12; Part III ch. 4, 5, 7, 9; Part IV introduction and ch. 1; Part V ch. 1, 8, 9; Preface principles 5 and 6. About 22,900 words of the roughly 105,000 in the body.
selection.advice: The book makes claims about children's health, diet, clothing, wet weather, brain activity and obedience. None is quoted or repeated. Where the workbook states a claim, it is attributed to Mason in her words and is about the parent's own conduct.
selection.note: Mason writes 'mother' throughout and about children under nine. The workbook says so on the Start screen and asks the reader to read it as parent.
selection.leftOut: Part I ch. 2 to 7 (including ch. 6 on diet, air and health); Part II ch. 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 13, 14; Part III ch. 1, 2, 3, 6, 8; Part IV ch. 2 to 8; Part V ch. 2 to 7 and 10 to 21; Part VI. These are teaching methods for a child, physiology, health advice or religious formation. The full list with reasons is in the workbook's internal.cut_log.
